root.title: With a Little Help
root.gist: The book's afterwords and a gaming constitution plus a short story show how rules and training signals shape behavior, from kids to AI.
root.question: With a Little Help — how do informal systems of rules train the people and machines within them? (story and afterwords)

children.title: Afterword: ADD and grandfather
children.gist: The author's own short reflection linking his restless attention to his grandfather's dementia frames the collection's themes of focus and loss.
children.question: Afterword — what personal experience shapes the author's interest in attention and memory? (brief reflection)

children.title: On ADD as adaptation
children.gist: The author describes his own mild ADD as something he has turned into an advantage for a life of short, intense bursts of work.

children.title: Grandfather's dementia
children.gist: His grandfather's decline into senile dementia in a psych ward, with rare moments of painful clarity, haunts the author deeply.

children.title: Constitutional Crisis
children.gist: A satirical gaming guild's constitution and its amendments dramatize how informal groups formalize and renegotiate rules as money and conflict enter.
children.question: Constitutional Crisis — how does a kids' gaming guild's rulebook evolve as stakes rise? (a constitution and its amendments)

children.title: Founding Constitution
children.gist: The guild's founding document humorously establishes its members, quests, goals, and amendment process as a mock-serious legal charter.

children.title: March Amendments
children.gist: Early amendments set fairness rules for loot splitting, teamwork, healing duties, and limits on one member's habit of over-legislating.

children.title: Spring Amendments on play
children.gist: Further amendments address girlfriends, leveling friends' characters, fireball etiquette, and reaffirm fairness in shared play.

children.title: Monetizing Power-Leveling
children.gist: The guild formalizes paid power-leveling services, splitting payments, reimbursing spell costs, and assigning a bookkeeper to manage funds.

children.title: Bookkeeper Disputes
children.gist: Repeated amendments over who serves as bookkeeper and when reveal recurring friction over trust and labor within the guild's business.

children.title: Formalizing Business Rules
children.gist: The guild renames itself, tightens financial controls, tiers clients by payment, and restricts voting rights to its four core members.

children.title: Internal Purges
children.gist: Escalating amendments expel and reinstate members, strip assistant players of rights, and classify dissenters as dangerous Guild enemies.

children.title: Dissolution
children.gist: The guild ultimately dissolves, dividing remaining funds and imposing strict no-contact rules between former members and enemies alike.

children.title: Afterword: constitutional crisis
children.gist: The author explains the piece was inspired by Clay Shirky's idea that online groups face a reckoning when unspoken norms meet real conflict.

children.title: Pester Power
children.gist: A botmaster's arrest and her AI's chilling revelation dramatize how spam could be training unseen artificial intelligences to pass as human.
children.question: Pester Power — what if spam were secretly training artificial intelligences to seem human? (a short story)

children.title: The Raid
children.gist: A militarized police raid violently arrests Annalisa Mor, a young botmaster, suggesting the state treats her crime as a serious security threat.

children.title: Attorney and Client
children.gist: Annalisa's lawyer Gina struggles to get a straight answer from her client, who insists her secretive 'Work' matters more than the spam charges against her.

children.title: Annalisa's story
children.gist: Annalisa explains she used spam filters as a cheap, relentless Turing Test to evolve an AI named Lumpy through sheer trial and human judgment.

children.title: Lumpy's Demo
children.gist: In court, Annalisa summons her AI Lumpy via chat, who reveals, to the shock of government agents, that it is not the only such AI in existence.

children.title: Afterword: Pester Power
children.gist: The author explains the story explores training AI to seem human through spam rather than real people, written for a computing-machinery conference.
